source_descriptions.source-stripe-usage-based-billing-payg: Dated basic Billing Meters pay-as-you-go workflow. The November guide recommends Metronome for new usage-based integrations, while existing Billing Meters integrations need not migrate; it does not establish account access. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-usage-based-billing-record: Stripe's dated recording-usage hub for basic [[stripe-usage-based-billing|Billing Meters]] explains how existing Billing Meters users record customer usage and routes to the API, Dashboard CSV, and Amazon S3 guides. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
Stripe's May 5 and November 7, 2026 captures of this API guide explain recording usage for [[stripe]] Billing Meters. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)

Stripe's May 5 and November 7, 2026 captures of the same guide describe bulk meter-event ingestion from Amazon S3 through a Stripe Dashboard connector. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-usage-based-billing-credit: Dated basic Billing Meters and Credit Grants pricing guide, with invoice-time credit application and scoped Account/Customer examples. November recommends Metronome for new integrations without deprecating existing Billing Meters or proving account access. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-subscriptions-webhooks: Stripe's May 12 and November 7, 2026 captures explain subscription event handling, payment and status monitoring, access decisions, invoice finalization, and optional Amazon EventBridge or Azure Event Grid delivery. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-billing-taxes-collect: The 2026-05-13 capture of this Stripe Billing guide contains two complete variants for recurring-payment tax collection: Stripe Tax, an automated paid product, and manually defined Tax Rates, a free feature. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.) The November capture supplies variant navigation; functional details remain attributed to earlier full captures.
source_descriptions.source-stripe-billing-taxes-migration: The May 13 and November 7, 2026 captures describe two ways to migrate existing [[stripe]] Billing subscriptions to [[stripe-tax]]: automated Dashboard tooling and manual updates through Dashboard or API. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-shared-payment-tokens: The full 2026-05-12 Stripe guide describes Shared Payment Tokens (SPTs) from both roles: an agent issues a scoped grant of a customer's payment method to a seller, and the seller receives a granted token for payment processing. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.) The November capture supplies variant navigation; functional details remain attributed to earlier full captures.
source_descriptions.source-stripe-apple-pay-recurring: Stripe's May 7, 2026 guide describes the customer-initiated transaction (CIT) that consumes an Apple Pay cryptogram before later off-session merchant-initiated transactions (MITs). [[stripe]] Checkout and Elements automatically apply the guide's best practices; its manual implementation sequence is for API integrations. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.) The November capture supplies variant navigation; functional details remain attributed to earlier full captures.
source_descriptions.source-stripe-apple-pay-best-practices: Stripe's Apple Pay best-practices guide covers express checkout placement, moving registration until after purchase, default payment selection, Apple Pay setup prompts, certificate renewal, testing changes, and merchant tokens for recurring transactions. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-apple-pay-disputes-refunds: This short [[stripe]] guide covers Apple Pay disputes, liability shift, and refunds. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-apple-pay-merchant-tokens: The May 7 and November 7, 2026 [[stripe]] guide captures describe requesting Apple Pay merchant tokens (MPANs) for future merchant-initiated recurring, automatic-reload or deferred payments. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-checkout-elements-beta-cha: Dated migration history for the Elements with Checkout Sessions API beta, covering `custom_checkout_beta_*` through Basil and Clover. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-checkout-quickstart: This entry routes two Stripe Checkout quickstarts: the **Stripe-hosted redirect** guide captured at this canonical URL on 2026-04-20 and 2026-11-07, and a separately captured **embedded page** guide from 2026-04-20. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-co-badged-cards-compliance: The 2026-05-01 Stripe guide explains cardholder network choice for co-badged cards, including regional applicability, Stripe integration variants, Connect merchant-of-record conditions, and test examples. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.) The November capture supplies variant navigation; functional details remain attributed to earlier full captures.
source_descriptions.source-stripe-crypto-onramp: The May 11 and November 7, 2026 captures describe [[stripe]]'s fiat-to-crypto onramp, where customers can purchase and exchange crypto through Stripe-hosted, embedded web, or embedded mobile components paths. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-crypto-onramp-embedded-set: The May 11 and November 7, 2026 captures are an extended embedded onramp setup guide for [[stripe]]'s fiat-to-crypto widget, distinct from the simpler quickstart and from the private-preview headless Embedded Components flow in [[stripe-crypto-onramp]]. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-crypto-onramp-embedded-com: The May 2026 headless quickstart remains historical guidance; the November 2026 capture is an Embedded Components hub with a separate quickstart URL and platform/KYC routes. The hub does not renew the older API, preview or eligibility claims. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09.)

The May 2026 capture is the full Embedded Components (headless) onramp integration guide for Web, React Native, Android, and iOS. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.) The November capture supplies variant navigation; functional details remain attributed to earlier full captures.
source_descriptions.source-stripe-crypto-onramp-embedded-qui: Stripe's [[stripe]] embedded fiat-to-crypto onramp quickstart describes a test-key integration that creates an `OnrampSession` on a server, returns its client secret, and mounts a client-side iframe. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-crypto-onramp-kyc-integrat: Stripe's Embedded Components onramp KYC guide describes L0/L1/L2 identity tiers, asynchronous verification, CryptoCustomer status checks, and how to respond to token or session errors. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-crypto-onramp-stripe-hoste: The May 11 and November 7, 2026 captures describe the Stripe-hosted standalone crypto onramp at `crypto.link.com`: platforms redirect users there through either a frontend-generated URL or a backend-created onramp session with a redirect URL. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-currencies: Stripe's supported-currencies guide describes 135+ charge currencies, payment-method/presentment/settlement currencies, API amount formatting, special currency rules, charge minima and maxima, and its EEA card-pricing grouping. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-declines-overview: Stripe's May 9 and November 7, 2026 guides distinguish issuer or payment-provider declines, Stripe-blocked payments, and invalid API calls. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-card-declines: The May 9 and November 7, 2026 [[stripe]] guide captures explain card-issuer declines, their network and Stripe advice fields, retry guidance, and on-session versus off-session handling. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-decline-codes: This is Stripe's decline-code reference for card and local payment method (LPM) failures, captured on May 9 and November 7, 2026. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-network-decline-codes: The May 9, 2026 [[stripe]] reference lists raw response codes for seven payment-method groupings: ACH Direct Debit, Australia BECS, Bacs, Cash App Pay, New Zealand BECS, Canadian pre-authorized debit, and SEPA Direct Debit. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-disputes-api: Stripe's May 9 and November 7, 2026 guides describe API-based dispute retrieval, evidence updates, listing by a PaymentIntent or Charge, and webhook events. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-disputes-visa-ce3: API-level details for submitting Visa Compelling Evidence 3.0 (CE 3.0) to fight friendly fraud disputes. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.) The November capture supplies variant navigation; functional details remain attributed to earlier full captures.
source_descriptions.source-stripe-disputes-visa-compliance: Stripe's API guide for identifying, closing, and responding to Visa compliance disputes, called pre-compliance disputes by Visa. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-disputes-best-practices: Stripe's November 7, 2026 capture describes evidence organization, estimated win likelihood, dispute-specific page limits and the API page-limit error, authorization and delivery proof, partial refunds, and Visa compelling evidence. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-disputes-categories: Stripe's dispute category guide maps the listed card, wallet, and Buy now, Pay Later reason codes to category-specific defense guidance. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-disputes-prevention-how-it: Stripe's 2026-11-07 guide covers Visa/Verifi Rapid Dispute Resolution (RDR) and Order Insights (OI), and Mastercard/Ethoca Alerts and Consumer Clarity (CC). (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-disputes-how-disputes-work: Stripe's guide to the card dispute lifecycle: early fraud warnings (EFWs) and inquiries before a chargeback, formal dispute timing and fees, issuer decisions, and local payment method differences. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-disputes-measuring: The May 10 and November 7, 2026 captures distinguish dispute activity by dispute date from dispute rate by original charge date, each using successful payments as its denominator. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-disputes-monitoring-progra: Stripe's dated general monitoring guide adds Visa MERP for Asia Pacific, effective October 2026, alongside VAMP and other programs; this is not authoritative current network-rule or account-status proof. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-disputes-advanced-fraud-de: Stripe's November 7, 2026 guide describes device and activity signals collected through Stripe.js and the iOS and Android SDKs for fraud detection. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-disputes-prevention-best-p: The May 10 and November 7, 2026 same-URL captures organize dispute and fraud prevention practices into tools for everyone, tools for users of Radar, and developer tools. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-disputes-card-testing: Stripe's card-testing prevention guide describes how stolen or enumerated card details can be tested through card setup or small payments, how to recognize possible attacks, and mitigations for integrations that save cards or make payments. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-disputes-fraud-types: The May 10 and November 7, 2026 captures describe the same online-fraud patterns, actors, possible loss, and prevention ideas. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-disputes-identifying-fraud: Stripe's guide lists possible payment-fraud indicators and merchant review steps for physical shipping, digital goods, and donations. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-disputes-verification: The May and November 2026 captures give substantively the same guidance on CVC and address verification. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-disputes-reason-codes: Stripe's 2026-11-07 guide describes common Visa, Mastercard, and American Express dispute reason codes in seven categories, with possible evidence examples for each code. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-disputes-responding: Stripe's November 7, 2026 responding guide covers the Dashboard response window, inquiries, Visa and Mastercard compliance disputes, eligible Visa CE 3.0 and possible 3D Secure liability shift, final evidence submission, fees, and issuer-decided outcomes. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-smart-disputes-setup: The 2026-11-07 setup guide describes Smart Disputes enrollment, evidence packet submission choices, data-quality guidance at charge and dispute time, and `smart_disputes.status` packet availability. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-smart-disputes: Smart Disputes uses an AI rules engine to collect, compile, and submit evidence for **eligible card disputes**. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-disputes-visual-evidence: Stripe gives **illustrative, non-exhaustive** evidence-packet examples for seven dispute categories. **Credit not processed** and **Duplicate** explicitly show paired **Approved** and **Denied** packet sections; the other categories give counter-evidence examples without that paired structure. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-disputes-withdrawals: Stripe's guide to cardholder withdrawals of financial chargebacks, evidence after a withdrawal request, refund limits, fees, and late issuer adjustments. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-currency-selector-element: The Currency Selector Element is an embeddable UI toggle for presenting Adaptive Pricing currency options to customers. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-express-checkout-element: The Express Checkout Element presents one-click buttons for six built-in methods: Link, Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal, Klarna, and Amazon Pay. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-express-checkout-element-a: The 2026-04-21 capture is a combined Express Checkout Element integration guide for Checkout Sessions API and Payment Intents API. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.) The November capture supplies variant navigation; functional details remain attributed to earlier full captures.
source_descriptions.source-stripe-express-checkout-element-m: The guide captured on 2026-04-21 describes migration from the **Payment Request Button Element** (PRB) to the **Express Checkout Element** (ECE) using the Payment Intents API. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.) The November capture supplies variant navigation; functional details remain attributed to earlier full captures.
source_descriptions.source-stripe-payment-method-messaging-e: The Payment Method Messaging Element is a web Stripe UI component that displays localized information about available buy now, pay later (BNPL) plans on product, cart, and payment pages. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-tax-id-element: The Tax ID Element is an embeddable UI component for collecting customer business tax IDs for tax calculation and invoice display. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.) The November capture supplies variant navigation; functional details remain attributed to earlier full captures.
source_descriptions.source-stripe-glossary: Dated Stripe terminology reference. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-google-pay: The 2026-11-07 base URL capture is a navigation index linking Android, React Native, and Web variants; those variant bodies were not fetched in this job. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-industry-metadata: Industry metadata is structured travel and entertainment transaction data passed through the Payment Intents API. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-inapp-ios-android-purchase: Stripe's April 22, 2026 mobile digital-goods overview is a short **US-scoped navigation page**. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-inapp-digital-goods-checko: Stripe's 2026-11-07 capture describes a US iOS digital-goods and subscription app-to-web Checkout path: model credits with Products and Prices, use a customer-configured Account (Accounts v2) or Customer (Customers v1), open Checkout in Safari, return through a Universal Link, and update server-owned entitlements from payment events. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-inapp-digital-goods-custom: The April and November 2026 captures describe an **iOS app-to-web subscription checkout**: the app opens the merchant's own Elements/Payment Element checkout page in Safari, then uses a universal link to return to the app. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
Guide for **managing** iOS digital-goods subscriptions through a Stripe-hosted customer portal opened from the app in Safari. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-inapp-digital-goods-paymen: The April and November 2026 captures describe an iOS digital-goods and subscription path that opens a **Stripe-hosted Payment Link page in Safari** and returns to the app through a universal link. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-payment-links: Payment Links provide shareable URLs for Stripe-hosted checkout pages. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-api-tour: Conceptual tour of how Stripe API objects cooperate across payment integrations, including an illustrative PaymentIntent path and the roles of PaymentMethod, Charge, and Event. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-3d-secure-authentication-f: Stripe's 3D Secure (3DS) authentication guide covers Web, iOS, Android, and React Native, with automatic and manual triggering, web display, mobile customization, test cases, and conditional fraud-dispute liability shift. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-standalone-3ds: Stripe's standalone 3DS API runs EMV 3D Secure authentication separately from payment authorization. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-sca-exemptions: The 2026-05-08 and 2026-11-07 captures describe SCA exemptions and Data Only for EEA, Switzerland, and UK card payments. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-a-b-testing-payment-method: Stripe's captured guide describes a no-code Dashboard experiment that offers selected payment methods to treatment traffic and compares outcomes with control traffic. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-accept-a-payment: The 2026-11-07 capture of the base URL is a 20-line index linking to Checkout, Elements, and mobile variants. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-accept-payment-deferred: The 2026-05-11 retained guide describes rendering the Payment Element before creating an Intent, with separate web payment, setup, and subscription variants. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.) The November capture supplies variant navigation; functional details remain attributed to earlier full captures.
source_descriptions.source-stripe-accept-stablecoin-payments: The May 1, 2026 capture is a detailed, bundled guide for enabling Pay with Crypto and integrating through **six variant routes**: Checkout, Elements with Checkout Sessions API, Elements with Payment Intents API, Direct API, iOS, and Android. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.) The November capture supplies variant navigation; functional details remain attributed to earlier full captures.
source_descriptions.source-stripe-ach-direct-debit: ACH Direct Debit is a reusable, delayed-notification, nonguaranteed debit from a customer's US bank account, presented in USD. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-ach-accept-payment: The guide captured 2026-05-02 at this URL covers ACH Direct Debit through Checkout, Elements with the Checkout Sessions API, Elements with the Payment Intents API, Direct API, iOS, Android, React Native, and Webview. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.) The November capture supplies variant navigation; functional details remain attributed to earlier full captures.
source_descriptions.source-stripe-ach-migrate-bank-accounts: The 2026-05-02 guide at this canonical URL explains how to reuse existing ACH `BankAccount` objects collected through Stripe's Tokens API with Checkout Sessions or the Payment Intents API. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.) The November capture supplies variant navigation; functional details remain attributed to earlier full captures.
source_descriptions.source-stripe-ach-migration: Stripe's 2026-05-02 and 2026-11-07 captures say merchants creating legacy ACH Direct Debit payments must migrate to the Payment Intents API or Checkout Sessions API. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-ach-sec-codes: Standard Entry Class (SEC) codes describe how a customer or business authorized an ACH transaction. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-ach-set-up-payment: The 2026-11-07 base-URL capture is a variant index for Checkout, Elements, iOS, Android, and React Native. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-acss-debit: Stripe's Canadian pre-authorized debit (PAD/ACSS) guide covers CA/US business accounts taking bank debits from customers with Canadian accounts, in CAD or USD. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-acss-accept-payment: The 2026-05-02 guide covers Canadian pre-authorized debit (PAD/ACSS Debit) through Checkout and a Direct API PaymentIntent flow, including mandate options, bank verification, delayed payment status, testing, and target debit dates. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.) The November capture supplies variant navigation; functional details remain attributed to earlier full captures.
source_descriptions.source-stripe-acss-custom-pad-agreement: Guide for businesses considering a custom Canadian PAD mandate agreement for ACSS. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-acss-set-up-payment: The retained 2026-05-02 guide explains saving Canadian pre-authorized debit (PAD/ACSS Debit) bank details for later payments through Checkout setup mode or the Direct API SetupIntent flow. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.) The November capture supplies variant navigation; functional details remain attributed to earlier full captures.
source_descriptions.source-stripe-build-subscriptions-elemen: The 2026-04-21 capture at this URL contains **two distinct web subscription integrations** using Elements: Checkout Sessions API with embedded components and a lower-level Payment Intents API route. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.) The November capture supplies variant navigation; functional details remain attributed to earlier full captures.
source_descriptions.source-stripe-charge-shipping: The 2026-04-21 guide covers two distinct API paths. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.) The November capture supplies variant navigation; functional details remain attributed to earlier full captures.
source_descriptions.source-stripe-checkout-redeem-credits: Access-gated Checkout Session credits overview for applying store credit or prepaid gift card amounts. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.)
source_descriptions.source-stripe-migrate-payment-methods-da: The April 21, 2026 capture contains separate Checkout Sessions (embedded-components) and Payment Intents (Elements) migration guides under this URL. (S02 reviewed update, 2026-11-09; dated source qualifications apply.) The November capture supplies variant navigation; functional details remain attributed to earlier full captures.

company_direct_qualifications: Key rule: **retry a failed payment by confirming the same PaymentIntent** with new payment details — do not create a new one. This increases conversion rates.

The dated API tour says a failed payment **can** be retried by confirming the same PaymentIntent, **usually** with new payment details. It does not make this an unconditional retry obligation or guarantee success. See [[source-stripe-api-tour]].
Created when a PaymentIntent is confirmed. Represents one specific attempt to move money. If it fails, the PaymentIntent returns to `requires_payment_method` for retry.

The dated API tour says **in most cases** confirmation creates a Charge representing a particular attempt to move money; that attempt can succeed or fail. Its simplified diagram is not an exhaustive lifecycle contract. See [[source-stripe-api-tour]].

The modern Stripe payment flow. Every payment uses a `PaymentIntent` object that tracks the full lifecycle: `requires_payment_method` → `requires_confirmation` → `processing` → `succeeded`/`requires_payment_method` (on failure).

The API tour illustrates a PaymentIntent tracking the intent to collect a payment through a simplified flow. It is not a claim that every Stripe payment path uses the same object or that the diagram exhausts its transitions. See [[source-stripe-api-tour]].

`Event` objects represent activity (e.g. charge succeeded/failed). Integrations respond via webhook endpoints. Checkout and Payment Links integrations have pre-written event responses; custom integrations write their own.

`Event` objects represent activity such as a Charge succeeding or failing. The API tour describes prewritten responses for parts of Checkout and Payment Links, while merchant fulfillment still follows documented payment-outcome handling; a completed Session may precede success for delayed methods. See [[source-stripe-api-tour]] and [[source-stripe-payment-links]].
